chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: The Deluxe Cafe and King Jones the barker
summary: The Deluxe was a Chicago cafe, and its doorman King Jones went club to club announcing acts with an English accent.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now do you remember the Deluxe?
Izzy Shore -- from what I gather was the person who was proprietor of the Deluxe Cafe. Now it was called -- I think it was Deluxe Saloon and Billiards Club.
And there was this Cafe and a doorman name Jones, he used to stand outside.
Yeah, that's King Jones. That was King Jones.
Yes, they called him King Jones.
Uh-huh. And he used to be a sort of barker?
Yes. Well he went from club to club. As a barker, you know, he'd also announced the shows, attractions, the acts that would follow. He was just a loud-mouthed
guy, tried to talk with an English accent.
Yeah, he tried to talk with an English accent.
